disposition_reason: Table 2 prints mean ± SD potassium, calcium, chlorine, aluminum and phosphorus (ppm) by XRF for seven retail milk powders sold in Romania; lead, cadmium, arsenic and mercury were not measured.

study.design: Retail survey of milk powders by XRF
study.market: Romanian market, original packaging, seven producers
study.method: X-ray fluorescence (vacuum) with graphite-homogenized samples; four standards 10 ppm to 10%
lod: XRF detection limit 5 ppm in vacuum
study.qa: Triplicate determinations; no CRM or recovery reported

unresolved: No lead, cadmium, arsenic or mercury results; the title refers to toxic contaminants but only K, Ca, Cl, Al and P are reported.
The "AML" values are not referenced to any regulation and do not correspond to known food limits.
Aluminum at 3,090-4,950 ppm is implausibly high for milk powder; XRF with a generic protein matrix may be biased.
Sample collection dates not stated; P5 appears to be a formulated (possibly infant) product but is not described as infant formula.
PDF access URL is an MDPI link; printed DOI 10.22543/7674.82.P237244 matches the manifest.
